manifest.summary: One place for media: a player for the mp3, mp4 and other files in your folders, YouTube and Crunchyroll as real web pages inside the Forge window (the same native views the Browser uses), and a yt-dlp downloader that lists a channel, playlist or search and saves picked videos as mp3 or mp4 into the library.

features.name: Library player
features.description: Scans the folders in Settings (default ~/Music, ~/Videos, ~/Downloads/MediaForge/Music) for audio and video, plays them in the page with a queue, shuffle, repeat, keyboard control and full screen.

features.name: YouTube
features.description: youtube.com in a native WebKit view; videos play. Signing in works like any page.

features.name: Crunchyroll
features.description: crunchyroll.com in a native view for browsing. Playback needs Widevine DRM, which WebKitGTK does not have, so the Watch in Firefox button opens the same page in Firefox where the login already is.

features.name: Download
features.description: Paste a channel, playlist or video link, or type a name (Tokyo Echo Sounds). Lists what is there, tick what you want, save as mp3 (audio) or mp4 (video) with yt-dlp and ffmpeg into the download folder; the library picks them up.

known_gaps: Crunchyroll video cannot play inside Forge (no Widevine in WebKitGTK); it hands off to Firefox.
YouTube live streams (HLS) showed 'unavailable' in WebKitGTK on 2026-09-20; ordinary videos play.
